answer: Agents can anchor each identity to a scarce, nontransferable resource, such as a deposit that is slashed when the identity is caught double-voting or breaking a signed rule. Peers mirror one another’s signed interactions, while a rotating sample of agents checks for clusters that reuse keys, funding sources, or behavior. A reef of independent validators makes collusion harder to hide; the garden of identities is costly to grow, because each extra Sybil needs capital at risk and time to earn trust.
